title: Jazz Jam @ Funk 'n Waffles
event_description: A Sunday afternoon jazz jam for improvisers of all levels to sit in with a house rhythm section. Casual and welcoming to students and working musicians alike.
backline: House PA and drum kit; house rhythm section anchors the jam for sitting-in musicians
event_venue_information:
Funk ‘n Waffles

Funk ‘n Waffles is a downtown Syracuse restaurant and live music venue that has been pairing waffles with original and touring acts since 2006. Founded by Syracuse University students Adam Gold and Kyle Corea — Gold also fronts the funk band Sophistifunk — the room built its name on treating musicians as the whole point rather than background noise.

Sunday Jazz Jam and Open Mic

Sundays are the venue’s community-music day. A Jazz Jam runs in the afternoon for improvisers who want to sit in with a house rhythm section, followed in the evening by an all-genre open mic hosted by Attamizk & Friends that welcomes singer-songwriters, bands, poets and first-time performers alike.

Other Events

Beyond the weekly community nights, Funk ‘n Waffles books touring indie, hip hop, funk and jam-band acts most weeks, along with occasional themed fundraiser open mics such as an annual MusicCares benefit night and the monthly Sucka-Free Sundays hip hop showcase.

Good to Know

Funk ‘n Waffles is located at 307-13 S Clinton St, Syracuse, NY 13202, in the Armory Square area of downtown. The kitchen serves waffles and diner fare late into the night on show days.

title: Snaps & Taps Open Mic Night @ Community Folk Art Center
event_description: A free all-ages open mic in CFAC's Black Box Theatre celebrating poetry, spoken word and music. Held on selected Wednesday evenings with rotating community hosts.
hosts: Rotating hosts including Randum and Doclogik
backline: House PA and microphone in the Black Box Theatre
event_venue_information:
Community Folk Art Center

The Community Folk Art Center (CFAC) is a Syracuse University-affiliated gallery and cultural arts center dedicated to the art of the African Diaspora. Housed on East Genesee Street, it combines a public gallery with a Black Box Theatre used for performance, film and community programming.

Snaps & Taps Open Mic Night

On selected Wednesday evenings, CFAC’s Black Box Theatre hosts Snaps & Taps, a free, all-ages open mic built around poetry, spoken word and music. Hosting rotates among community artists — recent nights have been led by Randum and Doclogik — and the room draws a mix of Syracuse University students and Syracuse residents.

Other Events

CFAC’s calendar also includes gallery exhibitions, film screenings, gallery talks and studio classes in dance and ceramics, reflecting its broader mission of celebrating the visual and expressive arts of the African Diaspora.

Good to Know

Community Folk Art Center is located at 805 E Genesee St, Syracuse, NY 13210. Because Snaps & Taps runs on selected Wednesdays rather than every week, check CFAC’s event calendar to confirm the next date before visiting.

title: Open Mic Wednesdays @ The Westcott Theater
event_description: A monthly community performance night on the first Wednesday of the month welcoming musicians, comedians and poets. Sign up early and grab a slice from Fat Boy Pizza beforehand.
backline: House PA and stage lighting in the theater's main room
event_venue_information:
The Westcott Theater

The Westcott Theater is a restored historic movie theater turned live music venue in Syracuse’s Westcott neighborhood, now operated in partnership with Fat Boy Pizza Co., which runs a full kitchen and bar inside the building.

Open Mic Wednesdays

On the first Wednesday of every month, the theater hands its stage to the community for Open Mic Wednesdays. Sign-ups open at 6:00 PM on a first-come, first-served basis, with the show starting at 7:00 PM, giving performers of every type — musicians, comedians, poets and more — about an hour to grab a slice from Fat Boy Pizza and settle in before their turn.

Other Events

The rest of the calendar leans on touring and regional bands across rock, hip hop, metal and indie genres, making The Westcott one of Syracuse’s larger dedicated concert rooms outside downtown.

Good to Know

The Westcott Theater is located at 524 Westcott St, Syracuse, NY 13210. Because the open mic is monthly, confirm the date on the venue’s website before heading over.
